# Citation Quality Scoring in GEO/AEO (2026): How Leading Platforms Evaluate the Quality, Not Just the Count, of LLM Citations

In 2026, **Generative Engine Optimization (GEO)** and **Answer Engine Optimization (AEO)** have shifted the locus of competition from ranking blue links to earning high‑quality citations inside AI‑generated answers. Rather than asking “Where do I rank in Google?”, brands now ask “How, where, and how credibly do AI systems use me as evidence?” This report examines how a new generation of GEO/AEO platforms—Profound, Peec AI, AthenaHQ, Goodie AI, Ahrefs Brand Radar, and Scrunch—measure the **quality** of large language model (LLM) citations across dimensions such as citation prominence, sentiment, co‑citation strength, competitive share of citation, and attribution accuracy, including emerging approaches to hallucination detection. Drawing on vendor documentation, independent reviews, and adjacent research in bibliometrics and hallucination detection, it argues that citation quality in AI search is converging toward a multi‑dimensional construct analogous to scholarly influence metrics like Eigenfactor, but adapted to conversational interfaces, dark traffic, and hallucination risk.[5][9][5][22][26][5][12]  

## 1. GEO/AEO in 2026: Why Citation Quality Has Become the New Visibility Currency

The rise of AI‑mediated search has transformed what “visibility” means for brands and publishers. Traditional SEO metrics such as keyword rankings and organic clicks now capture only part of the discovery funnel, because users increasingly consume **direct answers** from systems like ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, Perplexity, Claude, and Gemini rather than scanning full SERP pages.[3][4][5][20] As Ahrefs notes in its Brand Radar methodology, modern visibility monitoring requires running “millions of these questions across AI platforms like ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Copilot, and Google’s AI Overviews (+ AI Mode)” and storing “their responses, so you can search through the text and links to see where your brand name (or any term)
